t211: Every shift starts with skepticism. These are the questions agencies and clients always ask — and what we've learned to answer.
t212: How is AI production different from traditional production?
t213: Traditional production: Casting → Location → Crew → Shoot → Post → 3–6 weeks, with budgets of VND 55–200 million for a 30s TVC (Vietnam market).
t214: AI production: Brief → Character setup → per-shot generation → Post. With the right scope and assets ready, the timeline is typically 7–10 days and can significantly cut logistics costs versus a traditional shoot. Hybrid/live action is still used when the brief needs real talent, a product demo or physical proof.
t215: When to use AI: concept testing (animatic), social content, key visuals, storyboards. When you still need to shoot: broadcast 4K TVC, talent-driven campaign, complex product demo.
t216: 📖 Lemonlight: AI Video vs Traditional — An Honest Comparison
t217: Why does an AI commercial need per-shot production instead of generating a whole sequence?
t218: Because agencies and clients don’t approve “is the AI impressive” — they approve casting, product, claim, packshot, legal, lighting and continuity. Each element can change independently after a round of feedback.
t219: Per-shot production isolates exactly what needs fixing: shot 3 relights, shot 5 swaps talent, the end-frame adjusts the packshot — approved shots stay intact. That keeps scope, timeline and revision cost easier to control, while protecting what the brand needs the audience to remember: product, claim, packshot and CTA.
t220: One-take / multishot generation is still very useful for concept exploration, social experiments or a locked sequence. But when a project carries many approval rounds and brand accountability, the per-shot workflow is the safer architecture.
t221: → The difference isn’t who is “better at AI,” but whether the workflow is optimized for creative speed or for control and commercial accountability.
t222: What are the current technical limits of AI video?
t223: • Resolution: native 4K is available on current video models, or via upscale — 1080p remains the cost/quality sweet spot for digital and social; 4K for hero or broadcast carries a surcharge
t224: • Clip length: 10–15 seconds is routine, up to ~30s on some models — longer films are still cut from multiple clips, for shot-level control rather than because of the limit
t225: • Still hard to control: exact on-screen text, hands and fingers, small fast-moving objects, and the body of thick liquids
t226: • Randomness: the same prompt can yield different results — iteration is needed to reach the target quality
t227: • Content policy: Some AI platforms restrict content involving children or violence — the team will advise an alternative approach
t228: 📖 Cliptics: Video Quality — AI Generated vs Filmed Content
t229: Can a character’s face stay consistent throughout?
t230: Yes — but the quality depends on the input data:
t231: • With a talent reference shoot (40–80 photos per character) → very high face consistency, little iteration
t232: • With only reference photos from the agency → still achievable but needs more iteration
t233: This is why we recommend a talent reference shoot — it raises quality and provides a talent release for safe publishing.
t234: Image rights and AI law in Vietnam?
t235: Image rights: an AI character may carry facial features from a reference. To publish safely:
t236: ✅ Photoshoot real talent + sign a talent release
t238: If the agency supplies the reference photos → the agency is responsible for confirming usage rights.
t239: AI labeling: under Vietnam’s Artificial Intelligence Law (134/2025/QH15, in force since 01/03/2026), AI-generated content must be labeled on release. AI Studio advises on compliant labeling.
t240: 📖 Vietnam AI Law 134/2025 — Vietnam Legal Library
t241: What if the creative direction changes midway?
t242: Unlike traditional production (where you can reshoot a single angle), changing the concept in AI means all footage has to be regenerated from scratch. Cost and time are equivalent to starting over.
t243: → We recommend locking the creative direction before generation begins. Fine-tuning feedback (color, pace, timing) along the way is expected — it doesn’t require regenerating footage.
t244: What is an AI animatic for? Does it replace the traditional animatic?
t245: It can replace a traditional illustrated animatic when the goal is photoreal concept validation — but it does not replace every form of previs. An AI animatic lets teams test story, performance, camera and production design before committing budget to a shoot; because it looks closer to the intended film, client feedback becomes more specific and decisions become faster.
t246: Once the concept is approved → it can move to a real shoot (with clear direction) or be developed further in AI into a social film.
t247: 📸 Why shoot talent references for AI production?
t248: A talent reference shoot (40–80 photos per character) delivers:
t249: ✅ Significantly higher face consistency across shots
t250: ✅ A talent release → safe, legally compliant publishing
t251: ✅ Fewer revisions → saves time for both sides
t253: Reference-shoot cost: quoted by number of talent. It's an add-on service — not mandatory but strongly recommended for projects intended for release.
